work_rules.authority: Employment Act 1955 First Schedule paras 1A, 2 and 3, as substituted by the Employment (Amendment of First Schedule) Order 2022 [P.U. (A) 262], in operation 1 January 2023 — the ladder in ss.60(3), 60A(3), 60D(3) and 60D(4) does not apply to a person whose wages exceed RM4,000 a month, save for the para 2 categories, which are covered irrespective of wages; para 2(4) vessel work is outside Part XII altogether; "wages" is the s.2 definition less commissions, subsistence allowance and overtime payment. The rest break is s.60A(1)(a): an employee shall not be required to work more than five consecutive hours without a period of leisure of not less than thirty minutes; proviso (i) a break of less than thirty minutes does not break the continuity of the five hours, proviso (ii) work that must be carried on continuously may run eight consecutive hours inclusive of not less than forty-five minutes in the aggregate for a meal. The weekly rest day is s.59(1): every employee shall be allowed in each week a rest day of one whole day as determined from time to time by the employer, and where more than one is allowed the LAST is the rest day for the purposes of Part XII; s.59(1A) treats any continuous period of not less than thirty hours as a rest day for shift work. holiday_rest_precedence is SUBSTITUTE on the s.60D(1) proviso: where a gazetted public holiday falls on a rest day, or on another public holiday, the working day next following is a paid holiday in substitution. APPLIED: (a) the s.60A(1)(b)-(d) statement of normal hours — not more than eight hours in one day ("normal_day"), a spread-over of not more than ten hours ("spread_day") and not more than forty-five hours in one week ("weekly_total") — enforced as schedule limits, while every BEYOND_NORMAL band below prices the overtime it derives; Applied 2026-09-18: s.60A(1)(b) the normal day is 8 hours, or up to 9 under the proviso where the contracted week is within 45 (`normal_hours`); s.60A(1)(d) 45 hours a week is a ceiling on normal hours, the hours beyond it overtime (`weekly_normal`, read by payroll), not a wall on the roster; s.60(3)(a) rest-day work of a daily- or hourly-rated employee pays one day’s wages up to half the normal hours and two days’ beyond (`person.terms.pay_frequency`); s.59(1A) the rest day does not run during maternity, sick or hospitalisation leave (`weekly_rest_rule.suspended_by_leave`); First Schedule para 2(5): a domestic employee is outside ss.60–60F and the overtime ladder (`employment.type != "DOMESTIC"`). Applied 2026-09-23 (round 2): the s.60A(7) daily limit `daily_total` is twelve WORKED hours (s.60A(9) defines hours of work as time at the employer’s disposal), not twelve clock hours less the break. Nihon’s incentive boundary is the company’s own eleven hours’ total work in a day, stated as `funnel_above_hours: "11.0"` rather than read off the statutory limit.

wages.authority: Applied 2026-09-19 (2): Minimum Wages Order 2024 para 2: a domestic employee is outside the Order. Applied 2026-09-23 (audit): Minimum Wages Order 2024 [P.U.(A) 376/2024] paras 3(1) and 5(1) print a daily rate by the number of working days in a week — RM65.38 (six), RM78.46 (five), RM98.08 (four) — and RM8.72 an hour. The run compares a daily contract as the month it makes (the rate × the 26-day divisor), so `scale` restates the printed daily rate as that month over the printed monthly RM1,700; `hourly_by_region` holds an hourly rate to RM8.72 directly (the three figures are one table of the Order and move together); a monthly contract is the monthly RM1,700 (scale 1). Para 2 excludes only a domestic servant; the INTERN exclusion rests on an intern on industrial training not being employed under a contract of service.

encashment.authority: Employment Act 1955 ss.2, 60E(3A), 60I(1A)-(1B): monthly wages / 26; weekly basic / 6. Contract allowances are monthly amounts, so qualifying normal-hours allowances add their monthly amount / 26. Excluded payments do not enter the rate.; s.60I(1C) for daily/hourly rates (preceding wage period)

ordinary_rate_reference.authority: Employment Act 1955 s.60I(1C): total wages in the preceding wage period over the days actually worked

deduction_ceiling.authority: Employment Act 1955 s.24(8): the total deducted under s.24 in a month may not exceed 50% of the wages earned in that month — s.24(2)(d) deductions authorized by another written law (EPF, SOCSO, EIS, MTD) are deductions under the section, and s.24(2)(c)/(4)(b) advance and loan recoveries count; s.24(9)(b) excludes from the limit only “deductions from the final payment of the wages of an employee for any amount due to the employer and remaining unpaid by the employee on the termination of the employee’s contract of service” — the loan and advance recoveries; the statutory and other deductions on the final payslip stay within the half (round 5, Act 265 reprint as at 1 August 2023). Not applied: s.24(9)(a) (the s.13(1) indemnity) and s.24(9)(c) (a housing loan up to a further 25% with the Director General's written permission). Settled 2026-09-23 (round 4) from the Act 265 reprint as at 1 August 2023: s.24(1) “No deductions shall be made by an employer from the wages of an employee otherwise than in accordance with this Act”; s.24(2) “It shall be lawful for an employer to make the following deductions: … (d) deductions authorized by any other written law”; s.24(8) “The total of any amounts deducted under this section from the wages of an employee in respect of any one month shall not exceed fifty per centum of the wages earned by that employee in that month.” A statutory deduction (EPF employee share, SOCSO, EIS, MTD/PCB) is lawful only through s.24(2)(d) — s.24(1) admits no other route — so it is deducted under this section and counts toward the half; s.24(9) exempts it nowhere. The statutory charges are never shortened: they take their room first and only the counted recoveries are dropped.

final_pay_deadlines.authority: Employment Act 1955 s.21(2): an employee who terminates without notice under s.13(1)-(2) or s.14(3) is paid not later than the third day after the termination

Employment Act 1955 s.20 (a contract ending under s.11(1) or by notice under s.12, from either party) and s.21(1) (the employer terminating without notice): not later than the day the contract terminates

sources.instructions:
Sources are the primary instrument first — the statute or regulation in the national law database, the gazette, or the table the authority itself publishes — one page per fact the version seals, never a news article or a commentary. A historical version lists the instruments in force on its own effective date. Where the primary host refuses the reader (sso.agc.gov.sg, officialgazette.gov.ph, peraturan.bpk.go.id, kwsp.gov.my, hrdcorp.gov.my answer 403 to Norbital-Public-Page-Reader) the authority’s own published table is listed instead, or the Wayback Machine’s dated copy of the authority’s own page or PDF (web.archive.org/web/<timestamp>id_/<url>) — never a host the reader cannot open.
lom.agc.gov.my — Laws of Malaysia (AGC): every Act and gazette order. The consolidated reprint of a principal Act is /ilims/upload/portal/akta/LOM/EN/Act <n>.pdf (452 EPF, 4 SOCSO, 265 Employment, 53 Income Tax; text); an amending Act is a PDF at /ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputaktap/<id>_BI/<Act name>.pdf; a P.U.(A)/(B) order at /ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputp/<id>/PUB <n> (<year>).pdf. Use the exact PDF URL listed; the portal search is script-driven and not readable.
kwsp.gov.my — EPF. /en/employer/responsibilities/mandatory-contribution states the Part A/C/E rates, the age gates and the age-75 stop (HTML). /documents/d/guest/third_schedule_from_-1-october-2025 is the Third Schedule download link (the reader gets a shell page; the 1,203-row table is the PDF behind it). /en/employer/responsibilities/non-malaysian-citizen-employees is Part F.
perkeso.gov.my — SOCSO, EIS, SKBBK. /en/rate-of-contribution.html carries the Act 4 / Act 800 tables; /images/lindung/lindung-24-jam/NewContributionRateIncludingSKBBK.pdf is the 65-row table with the SKBBK column (0.2 MB, text); /en/skim-kemalangan-bukan-bencana-kerja-lindung-24-jam.html holds the SKBBK notice and FAQ PDF.
hasil.gov.my — LHDN MTD. /majikan/jadual-pcb-dan-spesifikasi-data/ lists the yearly "Spesifikasi Kaedah Pengiraan Berkomputer PCB <year>" PDF (/wp-content/uploads/spesifikasi-kaedah-pengiraan-berkomputer-pcb-<year>.pdf, 1.3 MB, text): Table 1 rates, reliefs, the RM10 minimum.
jtksm.mohr.gov.my — Employment Act 1955 reprint: /sites/default/files/2023-11/Akta Kerja 1955 (Akta 265).pdf (1.4 MB, text): ss.60, 60A, 60D, 60E, 60F, First Schedule. /ms/soalan-lazim/akta-kerja-1955-pindaan-2022 is the 2022 amendment FAQ.
gajiminimum.mohr.gov.my — the Minimum Wages Order in force, as one figure on the landing page.
hrdcorp.gov.my — HRD levy; the site sits behind a browser challenge the reader cannot pass, so note it rather than reading it.
johor.gov.my/rakyat/cuti-umum-2 — the Johor state holiday list for the year.

Finding changes (read these before comparing, every run):
1) lom.agc.gov.my: open subsid.php?type=pua, subsid.php?type=pub and principal.php?type=amendment (JS tables, newest first) plus the home page's 7-day What's New. Title search by URL (JS results, relevance order, scan every row for the year): search.php?search=<words>&kategori=iagcpuab_pua|iagcpuab_pub|iagcact_amendment|all&sorting=newest&lookup=title. Queries: 'minimum wages', 'employees provident fund', 'employees social security', 'employment insurance system', 'income tax (deduction from remuneration)', 'employment', 'holidays', 'human resources development'. Read the commencement clause, and check P.U.(B) for appointed dates of NOT YET IN FORCE Acts. Updated Acts: principal.php?type=updated. 2) LHDN: pengumuman-kenyataan-media and ketetapan-umum; PCB spec on majikan/jadual-pcb-dan-spesifikasi-data. 3) PERKESO directives-circulars. 4) KWSP highlights (browser). 5) JTKSM kenyataan-media for ad hoc state holidays; kabinet.gov.my for the yearly schedule. 6) Budget: belanjawan.mof.gov.my (October). hrdcorp.gov.my sits behind a Cloudflare challenge; do not attempt it; use PSMB Act/P.U.(A) on LOM. Discovery only: https://taxsummaries.pwc.com/malaysia/individual/significant-developments — then cite the gazette or agency page.

exit_facts.label: Leaving Malaysia for more than three months
exit_facts.description: Income Tax Act 1967 s.83(4): the employer gives CP21 notice and withholds money payable under s.83(5).

exit_facts.label: Wages of the last twelve months
exit_facts.description: Termination and Lay-Off Benefits Regulations 1980 reg.6(2): the s.2 wages earned in the twelve completed months before termination, stated where earlier payslips in this workspace do not hold them (an employee brought over with history). Absent, the termination benefit reads the payslips.

exit_facts.label: Dismissed for misconduct

work_rules.authority: Employment Act 1955 First Schedule paras 1A, 2 and 3, as substituted by the Employment (Amendment of First Schedule) Order 2022 [P.U. (A) 262], in operation 1 January 2023 — the ladder in ss.60(3), 60A(3), 60D(3) and 60D(4) does not apply to a person whose wages exceed RM4,000 a month, save for the para 2 categories, which are covered irrespective of wages; para 2(4) vessel work is outside Part XII altogether; "wages" is the s.2 definition less commissions, subsistence allowance and overtime payment. The rest break is s.60A(1)(a): an employee shall not be required to work more than five consecutive hours without a period of leisure of not less than thirty minutes; proviso (i) a break of less than thirty minutes does not break the continuity of the five hours, proviso (ii) work that must be carried on continuously may run eight consecutive hours inclusive of not less than forty-five minutes in the aggregate for a meal. The weekly rest day is s.59(1): every employee shall be allowed in each week a rest day of one whole day as determined from time to time by the employer, and where more than one is allowed the LAST is the rest day for the purposes of Part XII; s.59(1A) treats any continuous period of not less than thirty hours as a rest day for shift work. holiday_rest_precedence is SUBSTITUTE on the s.60D(1) proviso: where a gazetted public holiday falls on a rest day, or on another public holiday, the working day next following is a paid holiday in substitution. APPLIED: (a) the s.60A(1)(b)-(d) statement of normal hours — not more than eight hours in one day ("normal_day"), a spread-over of not more than ten hours ("spread_day") and not more than forty-five hours in one week ("weekly_total") — enforced as schedule limits, while every BEYOND_NORMAL band below prices the overtime it derives; Applied 2026-09-18: s.60A(1)(b) the normal day is 8 hours, or up to 9 under the proviso where the contracted week is within 45 (`normal_hours`); s.60A(1)(d) 45 hours a week is a ceiling on normal hours, the hours beyond it overtime (`weekly_normal`, read by payroll), not a wall on the roster; s.60(3)(a) rest-day work of a daily- or hourly-rated employee pays one day’s wages up to half the normal hours and two days’ beyond (`person.terms.pay_frequency`); s.59(1A) the rest day does not run during maternity, sick or hospitalisation leave (`weekly_rest_rule.suspended_by_leave`); First Schedule para 2(5): a domestic employee is outside ss.60–60F and the overtime ladder (`employment.type != "DOMESTIC"`). Applied 2026-09-23 (round 2): the s.60A(7) daily limit `daily_total` is twelve WORKED hours (s.60A(9) defines hours of work as time at the employer’s disposal), not twelve clock hours less the break. Nihon’s incentive boundary is the company’s own eleven hours’ total work in a day, stated as `funnel_above_hours: "11.0"` rather than read off the statutory limit.

wages.authority: Applied 2026-09-19 (2): Minimum Wages Order 2024 para 2: a domestic employee is outside the Order. Applied 2026-09-23 (audit): Minimum Wages Order 2024 [P.U.(A) 376/2024] paras 3(1) and 5(1) print a daily rate by the number of working days in a week — RM65.38 (six), RM78.46 (five), RM98.08 (four) — and RM8.72 an hour. The run compares a daily contract as the month it makes (the rate × the 26-day divisor), so `scale` restates the printed daily rate as that month over the printed monthly RM1,700; `hourly_by_region` holds an hourly rate to RM8.72 directly (the three figures are one table of the Order and move together); a monthly contract is the monthly RM1,700 (scale 1). Para 2 excludes only a domestic servant; the INTERN exclusion rests on an intern on industrial training not being employed under a contract of service.

encashment.authority: Employment Act 1955 ss.2, 60E(3A), 60I(1A)-(1B): monthly wages / 26; weekly basic / 6. Contract allowances are monthly amounts, so qualifying normal-hours allowances add their monthly amount / 26. Excluded payments do not enter the rate.; s.60I(1C) for daily/hourly rates (preceding wage period)

ordinary_rate_reference.authority: Employment Act 1955 s.60I(1C): total wages in the preceding wage period over the days actually worked

deduction_ceiling.authority: Employment Act 1955 s.24(8): the total deducted under s.24 in a month may not exceed 50% of the wages earned in that month — s.24(2)(d) deductions authorized by another written law (EPF, SOCSO, EIS, MTD) are deductions under the section, and s.24(2)(c)/(4)(b) advance and loan recoveries count; s.24(9)(b) excludes from the limit only “deductions from the final payment of the wages of an employee for any amount due to the employer and remaining unpaid by the employee on the termination of the employee’s contract of service” — the loan and advance recoveries; the statutory and other deductions on the final payslip stay within the half (round 5, Act 265 reprint as at 1 August 2023). Not applied: s.24(9)(a) (the s.13(1) indemnity) and s.24(9)(c) (a housing loan up to a further 25% with the Director General's written permission). Settled 2026-09-23 (round 4) from the Act 265 reprint as at 1 August 2023: s.24(1) “No deductions shall be made by an employer from the wages of an employee otherwise than in accordance with this Act”; s.24(2) “It shall be lawful for an employer to make the following deductions: … (d) deductions authorized by any other written law”; s.24(8) “The total of any amounts deducted under this section from the wages of an employee in respect of any one month shall not exceed fifty per centum of the wages earned by that employee in that month.” A statutory deduction (EPF employee share, SOCSO, EIS, MTD/PCB) is lawful only through s.24(2)(d) — s.24(1) admits no other route — so it is deducted under this section and counts toward the half; s.24(9) exempts it nowhere. The statutory charges are never shortened: they take their room first and only the counted recoveries are dropped.

sources.instructions:
Sources are the primary instrument first — the statute or regulation in the national law database, the gazette, or the table the authority itself publishes — one page per fact the version seals, never a news article or a commentary. A historical version lists the instruments in force on its own effective date. Where the primary host refuses the reader (sso.agc.gov.sg, officialgazette.gov.ph, peraturan.bpk.go.id, kwsp.gov.my, hrdcorp.gov.my answer 403 to Norbital-Public-Page-Reader) the authority’s own published table is listed instead, or the Wayback Machine’s dated copy of the authority’s own page or PDF (web.archive.org/web/<timestamp>id_/<url>) — never a host the reader cannot open.
lom.agc.gov.my — Laws of Malaysia (AGC): every Act and gazette order. The consolidated reprint of a principal Act is /ilims/upload/portal/akta/LOM/EN/Act <n>.pdf (452 EPF, 4 SOCSO, 265 Employment, 53 Income Tax; text); an amending Act is a PDF at /ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputaktap/<id>_BI/<Act name>.pdf; a P.U.(A)/(B) order at /ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputp/<id>/PUB <n> (<year>).pdf. Use the exact PDF URL listed; the portal search is script-driven and not readable.
kwsp.gov.my — EPF. /en/employer/responsibilities/mandatory-contribution states the Part A/C/E rates, the age gates and the age-75 stop (HTML). /documents/d/guest/third_schedule_from_-1-october-2025 is the Third Schedule download link (the reader gets a shell page; the 1,203-row table is the PDF behind it). /en/employer/responsibilities/non-malaysian-citizen-employees is Part F.
perkeso.gov.my — SOCSO, EIS, SKBBK. /en/rate-of-contribution.html carries the Act 4 / Act 800 tables; /images/lindung/lindung-24-jam/NewContributionRateIncludingSKBBK.pdf is the 65-row table with the SKBBK column (0.2 MB, text); /en/skim-kemalangan-bukan-bencana-kerja-lindung-24-jam.html holds the SKBBK notice and FAQ PDF.
hasil.gov.my — LHDN MTD. /majikan/jadual-pcb-dan-spesifikasi-data/ lists the yearly "Spesifikasi Kaedah Pengiraan Berkomputer PCB <year>" PDF (/wp-content/uploads/spesifikasi-kaedah-pengiraan-berkomputer-pcb-<year>.pdf, 1.3 MB, text): Table 1 rates, reliefs, the RM10 minimum.
jtksm.mohr.gov.my — Employment Act 1955 reprint: /sites/default/files/2023-11/Akta Kerja 1955 (Akta 265).pdf (1.4 MB, text): ss.60, 60A, 60D, 60E, 60F, First Schedule. /ms/soalan-lazim/akta-kerja-1955-pindaan-2022 is the 2022 amendment FAQ.
gajiminimum.mohr.gov.my — the Minimum Wages Order in force, as one figure on the landing page.
hrdcorp.gov.my — HRD levy; the site sits behind a browser challenge the reader cannot pass, so note it rather than reading it.
johor.gov.my/rakyat/cuti-umum-2 — the Johor state holiday list for the year.

Finding changes (read these before comparing, every run):
1) lom.agc.gov.my: open subsid.php?type=pua, subsid.php?type=pub and principal.php?type=amendment (JS tables, newest first) plus the home page's 7-day What's New. Title search by URL (JS results, relevance order, scan every row for the year): search.php?search=<words>&kategori=iagcpuab_pua|iagcpuab_pub|iagcact_amendment|all&sorting=newest&lookup=title. Queries: 'minimum wages', 'employees provident fund', 'employees social security', 'employment insurance system', 'income tax (deduction from remuneration)', 'employment', 'holidays', 'human resources development'. Read the commencement clause, and check P.U.(B) for appointed dates of NOT YET IN FORCE Acts. Updated Acts: principal.php?type=updated. 2) LHDN: pengumuman-kenyataan-media and ketetapan-umum; PCB spec on majikan/jadual-pcb-dan-spesifikasi-data. 3) PERKESO directives-circulars. 4) KWSP highlights (browser). 5) JTKSM kenyataan-media for ad hoc state holidays; kabinet.gov.my for the yearly schedule. 6) Budget: belanjawan.mof.gov.my (October). hrdcorp.gov.my sits behind a Cloudflare challenge; do not attempt it; use PSMB Act/P.U.(A) on LOM. Discovery only: https://taxsummaries.pwc.com/malaysia/individual/significant-developments — then cite the gazette or agency page.

work_rules.authority: Employment Act 1955 First Schedule paras 1A, 2 and 3, as substituted by the Employment (Amendment of First Schedule) Order 2022 [P.U. (A) 262], in operation 1 January 2023 — the ladder in ss.60(3), 60A(3), 60D(3) and 60D(4) does not apply to a person whose wages exceed RM4,000 a month, save for the para 2 categories, which are covered irrespective of wages; para 2(4) vessel work is outside Part XII altogether; "wages" is the s.2 definition less commissions, subsistence allowance and overtime payment. The rest break is s.60A(1)(a): an employee shall not be required to work more than five consecutive hours without a period of leisure of not less than thirty minutes; proviso (i) a break of less than thirty minutes does not break the continuity of the five hours, proviso (ii) work that must be carried on continuously may run eight consecutive hours inclusive of not less than forty-five minutes in the aggregate for a meal. The weekly rest day is s.59(1): every employee shall be allowed in each week a rest day of one whole day as determined from time to time by the employer, and where more than one is allowed the LAST is the rest day for the purposes of Part XII; s.59(1A) treats any continuous period of not less than thirty hours as a rest day for shift work. holiday_rest_precedence is SUBSTITUTE on the s.60D(1) proviso: where a gazetted public holiday falls on a rest day, or on another public holiday, the working day next following is a paid holiday in substitution. APPLIED: (a) the s.60A(1)(b)-(d) statement of normal hours — not more than eight hours in one day ("normal_day"), a spread-over of not more than ten hours ("spread_day") and not more than forty-five hours in one week ("weekly_total") — enforced as schedule limits, while every BEYOND_NORMAL band below prices the overtime it derives; Applied 2026-09-18: s.60A(1)(b) the normal day is 8 hours, or up to 9 under the proviso where the contracted week is within 45 (`normal_hours`); s.60A(1)(d) 45 hours a week is a ceiling on normal hours, the hours beyond it overtime (`weekly_normal`, read by payroll), not a wall on the roster; s.60(3)(a) rest-day work of a daily- or hourly-rated employee pays one day’s wages up to half the normal hours and two days’ beyond (`person.terms.pay_frequency`); s.59(1A) the rest day does not run during maternity, sick or hospitalisation leave (`weekly_rest_rule.suspended_by_leave`); First Schedule para 2(5): a domestic employee is outside ss.60–60F and the overtime ladder (`employment.type != "DOMESTIC"`). Applied 2026-09-23 (round 2): the s.60A(7) daily limit `daily_total` is twelve WORKED hours (s.60A(9) defines hours of work as time at the employer’s disposal), not twelve clock hours less the break. Nihon’s incentive boundary is the company’s own eleven hours’ total work in a day, stated as `funnel_above_hours: "11.0"` rather than read off the statutory limit.

wages.authority: Applied 2026-09-19 (2): Minimum Wages Order 2024 para 2: a domestic employee is outside the Order. Applied 2026-09-23 (audit): Minimum Wages Order 2024 [P.U.(A) 376/2024] paras 3(1) and 5(1) print a daily rate by the number of working days in a week — RM65.38 (six), RM78.46 (five), RM98.08 (four) — and RM8.72 an hour. The run compares a daily contract as the month it makes (the rate × the 26-day divisor), so `scale` restates the printed daily rate as that month over the printed monthly RM1,700; `hourly_by_region` holds an hourly rate to RM8.72 directly (the three figures are one table of the Order and move together); a monthly contract is the monthly RM1,700 (scale 1). Para 2 excludes only a domestic servant; the INTERN exclusion rests on an intern on industrial training not being employed under a contract of service.

encashment.authority: Employment Act 1955 ss.2, 60E(3A), 60I(1A)-(1B): monthly wages / 26; weekly basic / 6. Contract allowances are monthly amounts, so qualifying normal-hours allowances add their monthly amount / 26. Excluded payments do not enter the rate.; s.60I(1C) for daily/hourly rates (preceding wage period)

ordinary_rate_reference.authority: Employment Act 1955 s.60I(1C): total wages in the preceding wage period over the days actually worked

deduction_ceiling.authority: Employment Act 1955 s.24(8): the total deducted under s.24 in a month may not exceed 50% of the wages earned in that month — s.24(2)(d) deductions authorized by another written law (EPF, SOCSO, EIS, MTD) are deductions under the section, and s.24(2)(c)/(4)(b) advance and loan recoveries count; s.24(9)(b) excludes from the limit only “deductions from the final payment of the wages of an employee for any amount due to the employer and remaining unpaid by the employee on the termination of the employee’s contract of service” — the loan and advance recoveries; the statutory and other deductions on the final payslip stay within the half (round 5, Act 265 reprint as at 1 August 2023). Not applied: s.24(9)(a) (the s.13(1) indemnity) and s.24(9)(c) (a housing loan up to a further 25% with the Director General's written permission). Settled 2026-09-23 (round 4) from the Act 265 reprint as at 1 August 2023: s.24(1) “No deductions shall be made by an employer from the wages of an employee otherwise than in accordance with this Act”; s.24(2) “It shall be lawful for an employer to make the following deductions: … (d) deductions authorized by any other written law”; s.24(8) “The total of any amounts deducted under this section from the wages of an employee in respect of any one month shall not exceed fifty per centum of the wages earned by that employee in that month.” A statutory deduction (EPF employee share, SOCSO, EIS, MTD/PCB) is lawful only through s.24(2)(d) — s.24(1) admits no other route — so it is deducted under this section and counts toward the half; s.24(9) exempts it nowhere. The statutory charges are never shortened: they take their room first and only the counted recoveries are dropped.

final_pay_deadlines.authority: Employment Act 1955 s.21(2): an employee who terminates without notice under s.13(1)-(2) or s.14(3) is paid not later than the third day after the termination

sources.instructions:
Sources are the primary instrument first — the statute or regulation in the national law database, the gazette, or the table the authority itself publishes — one page per fact the version seals, never a news article or a commentary. A historical version lists the instruments in force on its own effective date. Where the primary host refuses the reader (sso.agc.gov.sg, officialgazette.gov.ph, peraturan.bpk.go.id, kwsp.gov.my, hrdcorp.gov.my answer 403 to Norbital-Public-Page-Reader) the authority’s own published table is listed instead, or the Wayback Machine’s dated copy of the authority’s own page or PDF (web.archive.org/web/<timestamp>id_/<url>) — never a host the reader cannot open.
lom.agc.gov.my — Laws of Malaysia (AGC): every Act and gazette order. The consolidated reprint of a principal Act is /ilims/upload/portal/akta/LOM/EN/Act <n>.pdf (452 EPF, 4 SOCSO, 265 Employment, 53 Income Tax; text); an amending Act is a PDF at /ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputaktap/<id>_BI/<Act name>.pdf; a P.U.(A)/(B) order at /ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputp/<id>/PUB <n> (<year>).pdf. Use the exact PDF URL listed; the portal search is script-driven and not readable.
kwsp.gov.my — EPF. /en/employer/responsibilities/mandatory-contribution states the Part A/C/E rates, the age gates and the age-75 stop (HTML). /documents/d/guest/third_schedule_from_-1-october-2025 is the Third Schedule download link (the reader gets a shell page; the 1,203-row table is the PDF behind it). /en/employer/responsibilities/non-malaysian-citizen-employees is Part F.
perkeso.gov.my — SOCSO, EIS, SKBBK. /en/rate-of-contribution.html carries the Act 4 / Act 800 tables; /images/lindung/lindung-24-jam/NewContributionRateIncludingSKBBK.pdf is the 65-row table with the SKBBK column (0.2 MB, text); /en/skim-kemalangan-bukan-bencana-kerja-lindung-24-jam.html holds the SKBBK notice and FAQ PDF.
hasil.gov.my — LHDN MTD. /majikan/jadual-pcb-dan-spesifikasi-data/ lists the yearly "Spesifikasi Kaedah Pengiraan Berkomputer PCB <year>" PDF (/wp-content/uploads/spesifikasi-kaedah-pengiraan-berkomputer-pcb-<year>.pdf, 1.3 MB, text): Table 1 rates, reliefs, the RM10 minimum.
jtksm.mohr.gov.my — Employment Act 1955 reprint: /sites/default/files/2023-11/Akta Kerja 1955 (Akta 265).pdf (1.4 MB, text): ss.60, 60A, 60D, 60E, 60F, First Schedule. /ms/soalan-lazim/akta-kerja-1955-pindaan-2022 is the 2022 amendment FAQ.
gajiminimum.mohr.gov.my — the Minimum Wages Order in force, as one figure on the landing page.
hrdcorp.gov.my — HRD levy; the site sits behind a browser challenge the reader cannot pass, so note it rather than reading it.
johor.gov.my/rakyat/cuti-umum-2 — the Johor state holiday list for the year.

Finding changes (read these before comparing, every run):
1) lom.agc.gov.my: open subsid.php?type=pua, subsid.php?type=pub and principal.php?type=amendment (JS tables, newest first) plus the home page's 7-day What's New. Title search by URL (JS results, relevance order, scan every row for the year): search.php?search=<words>&kategori=iagcpuab_pua|iagcpuab_pub|iagcact_amendment|all&sorting=newest&lookup=title. Queries: 'minimum wages', 'employees provident fund', 'employees social security', 'employment insurance system', 'income tax (deduction from remuneration)', 'employment', 'holidays', 'human resources development'. Read the commencement clause, and check P.U.(B) for appointed dates of NOT YET IN FORCE Acts. Updated Acts: principal.php?type=updated. 2) LHDN: pengumuman-kenyataan-media and ketetapan-umum; PCB spec on majikan/jadual-pcb-dan-spesifikasi-data. 3) PERKESO directives-circulars. 4) KWSP highlights (browser). 5) JTKSM kenyataan-media for ad hoc state holidays; kabinet.gov.my for the yearly schedule. 6) Budget: belanjawan.mof.gov.my (October). hrdcorp.gov.my sits behind a Cloudflare challenge; do not attempt it; use PSMB Act/P.U.(A) on LOM. Discovery only: https://taxsummaries.pwc.com/malaysia/individual/significant-developments — then cite the gazette or agency page.

work_rules.authority: Employment Act 1955 First Schedule paras 1A, 2 and 3, as substituted by the Employment (Amendment of First Schedule) Order 2022 [P.U. (A) 262], in operation 1 January 2023 — the ladder in ss.60(3), 60A(3), 60D(3) and 60D(4) does not apply to a person whose wages exceed RM4,000 a month, save for the para 2 categories, which are covered irrespective of wages; para 2(4) vessel work is outside Part XII altogether; "wages" is the s.2 definition less commissions, subsistence allowance and overtime payment. The rest break is s.60A(1)(a): an employee shall not be required to work more than five consecutive hours without a period of leisure of not less than thirty minutes; proviso (i) a break of less than thirty minutes does not break the continuity of the five hours, proviso (ii) work that must be carried on continuously may run eight consecutive hours inclusive of not less than forty-five minutes in the aggregate for a meal. The weekly rest day is s.59(1): every employee shall be allowed in each week a rest day of one whole day as determined from time to time by the employer, and where more than one is allowed the LAST is the rest day for the purposes of Part XII; s.59(1A) treats any continuous period of not less than thirty hours as a rest day for shift work. holiday_rest_precedence is SUBSTITUTE on the s.60D(1) proviso: where a gazetted public holiday falls on a rest day, or on another public holiday, the working day next following is a paid holiday in substitution. APPLIED: (a) the s.60A(1)(b)-(d) statement of normal hours — not more than eight hours in one day ("normal_day"), a spread-over of not more than ten hours ("spread_day") and not more than forty-five hours in one week ("weekly_total") — enforced as schedule limits, while every BEYOND_NORMAL band below prices the overtime it derives; Applied 2026-09-18: s.60A(1)(b) the normal day is 8 hours, or up to 9 under the proviso where the contracted week is within 45 (`normal_hours`); s.60A(1)(d) 45 hours a week is a ceiling on normal hours, the hours beyond it overtime (`weekly_normal`, read by payroll), not a wall on the roster; s.60(3)(a) rest-day work of a daily- or hourly-rated employee pays one day’s wages up to half the normal hours and two days’ beyond (`person.terms.pay_frequency`); s.59(1A) the rest day does not run during maternity, sick or hospitalisation leave (`weekly_rest_rule.suspended_by_leave`); First Schedule para 2(5): a domestic employee is outside ss.60–60F and the overtime ladder (`employment.type != "DOMESTIC"`). Applied 2026-09-23 (round 2): the s.60A(7) daily limit `daily_total` is twelve WORKED hours (s.60A(9) defines hours of work as time at the employer’s disposal), not twelve clock hours less the break. Nihon’s incentive boundary is the company’s own eleven hours’ total work in a day, stated as `funnel_above_hours: "11.0"` rather than read off the statutory limit.

wages.authority: Applied 2026-09-19 (2): Minimum Wages Order 2024 para 2: a domestic employee is outside the Order. Applied 2026-09-23 (audit): Minimum Wages Order 2024 [P.U.(A) 376/2024] paras 3(1) and 5(1) print a daily rate by the number of working days in a week — RM65.38 (six), RM78.46 (five), RM98.08 (four) — and RM8.72 an hour. The run compares a daily contract as the month it makes (the rate × the 26-day divisor), so `scale` restates the printed daily rate as that month over the printed monthly RM1,700; `hourly_by_region` holds an hourly rate to RM8.72 directly (the three figures are one table of the Order and move together); a monthly contract is the monthly RM1,700 (scale 1). Para 2 excludes only a domestic servant; the INTERN exclusion rests on an intern on industrial training not being employed under a contract of service.

encashment.authority: Employment Act 1955 ss.2, 60E(3A), 60I(1A)-(1B): monthly wages / 26; weekly basic / 6. Contract allowances are monthly amounts, so qualifying normal-hours allowances add their monthly amount / 26. Excluded payments do not enter the rate.; s.60I(1C) for daily/hourly rates (preceding wage period)

ordinary_rate_reference.authority: Employment Act 1955 s.60I(1C): total wages in the preceding wage period over the days actually worked

deduction_ceiling.authority: Employment Act 1955 s.24(8): the total deducted under s.24 in a month may not exceed 50% of the wages earned in that month — s.24(2)(d) deductions authorized by another written law (EPF, SOCSO, EIS, MTD) are deductions under the section, and s.24(2)(c)/(4)(b) advance and loan recoveries count; s.24(9)(b) excludes from the limit only “deductions from the final payment of the wages of an employee for any amount due to the employer and remaining unpaid by the employee on the termination of the employee’s contract of service” — the loan and advance recoveries; the statutory and other deductions on the final payslip stay within the half (round 5, Act 265 reprint as at 1 August 2023). Not applied: s.24(9)(a) (the s.13(1) indemnity) and s.24(9)(c) (a housing loan up to a further 25% with the Director General's written permission). Settled 2026-09-23 (round 4) from the Act 265 reprint as at 1 August 2023: s.24(1) “No deductions shall be made by an employer from the wages of an employee otherwise than in accordance with this Act”; s.24(2) “It shall be lawful for an employer to make the following deductions: … (d) deductions authorized by any other written law”; s.24(8) “The total of any amounts deducted under this section from the wages of an employee in respect of any one month shall not exceed fifty per centum of the wages earned by that employee in that month.” A statutory deduction (EPF employee share, SOCSO, EIS, MTD/PCB) is lawful only through s.24(2)(d) — s.24(1) admits no other route — so it is deducted under this section and counts toward the half; s.24(9) exempts it nowhere. The statutory charges are never shortened: they take their room first and only the counted recoveries are dropped.

sources.instructions:
Sources are the primary instrument first — the statute or regulation in the national law database, the gazette, or the table the authority itself publishes — one page per fact the version seals, never a news article or a commentary. A historical version lists the instruments in force on its own effective date. Where the primary host refuses the reader (sso.agc.gov.sg, officialgazette.gov.ph, peraturan.bpk.go.id, kwsp.gov.my, hrdcorp.gov.my answer 403 to Norbital-Public-Page-Reader) the authority’s own published table is listed instead, or the Wayback Machine’s dated copy of the authority’s own page or PDF (web.archive.org/web/<timestamp>id_/<url>) — never a host the reader cannot open.
lom.agc.gov.my — Laws of Malaysia (AGC): every Act and gazette order. The consolidated reprint of a principal Act is /ilims/upload/portal/akta/LOM/EN/Act <n>.pdf (452 EPF, 4 SOCSO, 265 Employment, 53 Income Tax; text); an amending Act is a PDF at /ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputaktap/<id>_BI/<Act name>.pdf; a P.U.(A)/(B) order at /ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputp/<id>/PUB <n> (<year>).pdf. Use the exact PDF URL listed; the portal search is script-driven and not readable.
kwsp.gov.my — EPF. /en/employer/responsibilities/mandatory-contribution states the Part A/C/E rates, the age gates and the age-75 stop (HTML). /documents/d/guest/third_schedule_from_-1-october-2025 is the Third Schedule download link (the reader gets a shell page; the 1,203-row table is the PDF behind it). /en/employer/responsibilities/non-malaysian-citizen-employees is Part F.
perkeso.gov.my — SOCSO, EIS, SKBBK. /en/rate-of-contribution.html carries the Act 4 / Act 800 tables; /images/lindung/lindung-24-jam/NewContributionRateIncludingSKBBK.pdf is the 65-row table with the SKBBK column (0.2 MB, text); /en/skim-kemalangan-bukan-bencana-kerja-lindung-24-jam.html holds the SKBBK notice and FAQ PDF.
hasil.gov.my — LHDN MTD. /majikan/jadual-pcb-dan-spesifikasi-data/ lists the yearly "Spesifikasi Kaedah Pengiraan Berkomputer PCB <year>" PDF (/wp-content/uploads/spesifikasi-kaedah-pengiraan-berkomputer-pcb-<year>.pdf, 1.3 MB, text): Table 1 rates, reliefs, the RM10 minimum.
jtksm.mohr.gov.my — Employment Act 1955 reprint: /sites/default/files/2023-11/Akta Kerja 1955 (Akta 265).pdf (1.4 MB, text): ss.60, 60A, 60D, 60E, 60F, First Schedule. /ms/soalan-lazim/akta-kerja-1955-pindaan-2022 is the 2022 amendment FAQ.
gajiminimum.mohr.gov.my — the Minimum Wages Order in force, as one figure on the landing page.
hrdcorp.gov.my — HRD levy; the site sits behind a browser challenge the reader cannot pass, so note it rather than reading it.
johor.gov.my/rakyat/cuti-umum-2 — the Johor state holiday list for the year.

1) lom.agc.gov.my: open subsid.php?type=pua, subsid.php?type=pub and principal.php?type=amendment (JS tables, newest first) plus the home page's 7-day What's New. Title search by URL (JS results, relevance order, scan every row for the year): search.php?search=<words>&kategori=iagcpuab_pua|iagcpuab_pub|iagcact_amendment|all&sorting=newest&lookup=title. Queries: 'minimum wages', 'employees provident fund', 'employees social security', 'employment insurance system', 'income tax (deduction from remuneration)', 'employment', 'holidays', 'human resources development'. Read the commencement clause, and check P.U.(B) for appointed dates of NOT YET IN FORCE Acts. Updated Acts: principal.php?type=updated. 2) LHDN: pengumuman-kenyataan-media and ketetapan-umum; PCB spec on majikan/jadual-pcb-dan-spesifikasi-data. 3) PERKESO directives-circulars. 4) KWSP highlights (browser). 5) JTKSM kenyataan-media for ad hoc state holidays; kabinet.gov.my for the yearly schedule. 6) Budget: belanjawan.mof.gov.my (October). hrdcorp.gov.my sits behind a Cloudflare challenge; do not attempt it; use PSMB Act/P.U.(A) on LOM. Discovery only: https://taxsummaries.pwc.com/malaysia/individual/significant-developments — then cite the gazette or agency page.

work_rules.authority: Employment Act 1955 First Schedule paras 1A, 2 and 3, as substituted by the Employment (Amendment of First Schedule) Order 2022 [P.U. (A) 262], in operation 1 January 2023 — the ladder in ss.60(3), 60A(3), 60D(3) and 60D(4) does not apply to a person whose wages exceed RM4,000 a month, save for the para 2 categories, which are covered irrespective of wages; para 2(4) vessel work is outside Part XII altogether; "wages" is the s.2 definition less commissions, subsistence allowance and overtime payment. The rest break is s.60A(1)(a): an employee shall not be required to work more than five consecutive hours without a period of leisure of not less than thirty minutes; proviso (i) a break of less than thirty minutes does not break the continuity of the five hours, proviso (ii) work that must be carried on continuously may run eight consecutive hours inclusive of not less than forty-five minutes in the aggregate for a meal. The weekly rest day is s.59(1): every employee shall be allowed in each week a rest day of one whole day as determined from time to time by the employer, and where more than one is allowed the LAST is the rest day for the purposes of Part XII; s.59(1A) treats any continuous period of not less than thirty hours as a rest day for shift work. holiday_rest_precedence is SUBSTITUTE on the s.60D(1) proviso: where a gazetted public holiday falls on a rest day, or on another public holiday, the working day next following is a paid holiday in substitution. APPLIED: (a) the s.60A(1)(b)-(d) statement of normal hours — not more than eight hours in one day ("normal_day"), a spread-over of not more than ten hours ("spread_day") and not more than forty-five hours in one week ("weekly_total") — enforced as schedule limits, while every BEYOND_NORMAL band below prices the overtime it derives; Applied 2026-09-18: s.60A(1)(b) the normal day is 8 hours, or up to 9 under the proviso where the contracted week is within 45 (`normal_hours`); s.60A(1)(d) 45 hours a week is a ceiling on normal hours, the hours beyond it overtime (`weekly_normal`, read by payroll), not a wall on the roster; s.60(3)(a) rest-day work of a daily- or hourly-rated employee pays one day’s wages up to half the normal hours and two days’ beyond (`person.terms.pay_frequency`); s.59(1A) the rest day does not run during maternity, sick or hospitalisation leave (`weekly_rest_rule.suspended_by_leave`); First Schedule para 2(5): a domestic employee is outside ss.60–60F and the overtime ladder (`employment.type != "DOMESTIC"`). Applied 2026-09-23 (round 2): the s.60A(7) daily limit `daily_total` is twelve WORKED hours (s.60A(9) defines hours of work as time at the employer’s disposal), not twelve clock hours less the break. Nihon’s incentive boundary is the company’s own eleven hours’ total work in a day, stated as `funnel_above_hours: "11.0"` rather than read off the statutory limit.

wages.authority: Applied 2026-09-19 (2): Minimum Wages Order 2024 para 2: a domestic employee is outside the Order. Applied 2026-09-23 (audit): Minimum Wages Order 2024 [P.U.(A) 376/2024] paras 3(1) and 5(1) print a daily rate by the number of working days in a week — RM65.38 (six), RM78.46 (five), RM98.08 (four) — and RM8.72 an hour. The run compares a daily contract as the month it makes (the rate × the 26-day divisor), so `scale` restates the printed daily rate as that month over the printed monthly RM1,700; `hourly_by_region` holds an hourly rate to RM8.72 directly (the three figures are one table of the Order and move together); a monthly contract is the monthly RM1,700 (scale 1). Para 2 excludes only a domestic servant; the INTERN exclusion rests on an intern on industrial training not being employed under a contract of service.

encashment.authority: Employment Act 1955 ss.2, 60E(3A), 60I(1A)-(1B): monthly wages / 26; weekly basic / 6. Contract allowances are monthly amounts, so qualifying normal-hours allowances add their monthly amount / 26. Excluded payments do not enter the rate.; s.60I(1C) for daily/hourly rates (preceding wage period)

ordinary_rate_reference.authority: Employment Act 1955 s.60I(1C): total wages in the preceding wage period over the days actually worked

deduction_ceiling.authority: Employment Act 1955 s.24(8): the total deducted under s.24 in a month may not exceed 50% of the wages earned in that month — s.24(2)(d) deductions authorized by another written law (EPF, SOCSO, EIS, MTD) are deductions under the section, and s.24(2)(c)/(4)(b) advance and loan recoveries count; s.24(9)(b) excludes from the limit only “deductions from the final payment of the wages of an employee for any amount due to the employer and remaining unpaid by the employee on the termination of the employee’s contract of service” — the loan and advance recoveries; the statutory and other deductions on the final payslip stay within the half (round 5, Act 265 reprint as at 1 August 2023). Not applied: s.24(9)(a) (the s.13(1) indemnity) and s.24(9)(c) (a housing loan up to a further 25% with the Director General's written permission). Settled 2026-09-23 (round 4) from the Act 265 reprint as at 1 August 2023: s.24(1) “No deductions shall be made by an employer from the wages of an employee otherwise than in accordance with this Act”; s.24(2) “It shall be lawful for an employer to make the following deductions: … (d) deductions authorized by any other written law”; s.24(8) “The total of any amounts deducted under this section from the wages of an employee in respect of any one month shall not exceed fifty per centum of the wages earned by that employee in that month.” A statutory deduction (EPF employee share, SOCSO, EIS, MTD/PCB) is lawful only through s.24(2)(d) — s.24(1) admits no other route — so it is deducted under this section and counts toward the half; s.24(9) exempts it nowhere. The statutory charges are never shortened: they take their room first and only the counted recoveries are dropped.

final_pay_deadlines.authority: Employment Act 1955 s.21(2): an employee who terminates without notice under s.13(1)-(2) or s.14(3) is paid not later than the third day after the termination

sources.instructions:
Sources are the primary instrument first — the statute or regulation in the national law database, the gazette, or the table the authority itself publishes — one page per fact the version seals, never a news article or a commentary. A historical version lists the instruments in force on its own effective date. Where the primary host refuses the reader (sso.agc.gov.sg, officialgazette.gov.ph, peraturan.bpk.go.id, kwsp.gov.my, hrdcorp.gov.my answer 403 to Norbital-Public-Page-Reader) the authority’s own published table is listed instead, or the Wayback Machine’s dated copy of the authority’s own page or PDF (web.archive.org/web/<timestamp>id_/<url>) — never a host the reader cannot open.
lom.agc.gov.my — Laws of Malaysia (AGC): every Act and gazette order. The consolidated reprint of a principal Act is /ilims/upload/portal/akta/LOM/EN/Act <n>.pdf (452 EPF, 4 SOCSO, 265 Employment, 53 Income Tax; text); an amending Act is a PDF at /ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputaktap/<id>_BI/<Act name>.pdf; a P.U.(A)/(B) order at /ilims/upload/portal/akta/outputp/<id>/PUB <n> (<year>).pdf. Use the exact PDF URL listed; the portal search is script-driven and not readable.
kwsp.gov.my — EPF. /en/employer/responsibilities/mandatory-contribution states the Part A/C/E rates, the age gates and the age-75 stop (HTML). /documents/d/guest/third_schedule_from_-1-october-2025 is the Third Schedule download link (the reader gets a shell page; the 1,203-row table is the PDF behind it). /en/employer/responsibilities/non-malaysian-citizen-employees is Part F.
perkeso.gov.my — SOCSO, EIS, SKBBK. /en/rate-of-contribution.html carries the Act 4 / Act 800 tables; /images/lindung/lindung-24-jam/NewContributionRateIncludingSKBBK.pdf is the 65-row table with the SKBBK column (0.2 MB, text); /en/skim-kemalangan-bukan-bencana-kerja-lindung-24-jam.html holds the SKBBK notice and FAQ PDF.
hasil.gov.my — LHDN MTD. /majikan/jadual-pcb-dan-spesifikasi-data/ lists the yearly "Spesifikasi Kaedah Pengiraan Berkomputer PCB <year>" PDF (/wp-content/uploads/spesifikasi-kaedah-pengiraan-berkomputer-pcb-<year>.pdf, 1.3 MB, text): Table 1 rates, reliefs, the RM10 minimum.
jtksm.mohr.gov.my — Employment Act 1955 reprint: /sites/default/files/2023-11/Akta Kerja 1955 (Akta 265).pdf (1.4 MB, text): ss.60, 60A, 60D, 60E, 60F, First Schedule. /ms/soalan-lazim/akta-kerja-1955-pindaan-2022 is the 2022 amendment FAQ.
gajiminimum.mohr.gov.my — the Minimum Wages Order in force, as one figure on the landing page.
hrdcorp.gov.my — HRD levy; the site sits behind a browser challenge the reader cannot pass, so note it rather than reading it.
johor.gov.my/rakyat/cuti-umum-2 — the Johor state holiday list for the year.

Finding changes (read these before comparing, every run):
1) lom.agc.gov.my: open subsid.php?type=pua, subsid.php?type=pub and principal.php?type=amendment (JS tables, newest first) plus the home page's 7-day What's New. Title search by URL (JS results, relevance order, scan every row for the year): search.php?search=<words>&kategori=iagcpuab_pua|iagcpuab_pub|iagcact_amendment|all&sorting=newest&lookup=title. Queries: 'minimum wages', 'employees provident fund', 'employees social security', 'employment insurance system', 'income tax (deduction from remuneration)', 'employment', 'holidays', 'human resources development'. Read the commencement clause, and check P.U.(B) for appointed dates of NOT YET IN FORCE Acts. Updated Acts: principal.php?type=updated. 2) LHDN: pengumuman-kenyataan-media and ketetapan-umum; PCB spec on majikan/jadual-pcb-dan-spesifikasi-data. 3) PERKESO directives-circulars. 4) KWSP highlights (browser). 5) JTKSM kenyataan-media for ad hoc state holidays; kabinet.gov.my for the yearly schedule. 6) Budget: belanjawan.mof.gov.my (October). hrdcorp.gov.my sits behind a Cloudflare challenge; do not attempt it; use PSMB Act/P.U.(A) on LOM. Discovery only: https://taxsummaries.pwc.com/malaysia/individual/significant-developments — then cite the gazette or agency page.

obligations.description: SOCSO, EIS (and from 1 June 2026 SKBBK) contribution payment with the monthly data (ASSIST)
obligations.trigger: Wages payable for the month
obligations.timing: Not later than the 15th day of the following month; interest at 6% a year for each day unpaid thereafter
obligations.authority: Employees’ Social Security Act 1969 (Act 4) ss.6, 14A (https://www.perkeso.gov.my/images/akta/ACT%204/Act%204%20-%20EMPLOYEES%E2%80%99%20SOCIAL%20SECURITY%20ACT%201969%20%28As%20at%201%20September%202022%29.pdf); Employment Insurance System Act 2017 (Act 800) ss.18, 20, 21 (https://perkeso.gov.my/images/akta/ACT%20800/Akta%20800_EMPLOYMENT%20INSURANCE%20SYSTEM%20ACT%202017.pdf); PERKESO, Contribution Payment (https://www.perkeso.gov.my/en/contribution-payment.html)

obligations.description: SKBBK (LINDUNG 24 Jam) employee contribution deducted and paid with SOCSO
obligations.trigger: Every insured employee from 1 June 2026
obligations.timing: Phase 1 at 0.75% of wages on the Act 4 bands (years 1-2), 1.00% in years 3-5, 1.25% from year 6; paid with the month’s SOCSO by the 15th of the following month
obligations.authority: PERKESO, Skim Kemalangan Bukan Bencana Kerja (LINDUNG 24 Jam) (https://www.perkeso.gov.my/en/skim-kemalangan-bukan-bencana-kerja-lindung-24-jam.html); NewContributionRateIncludingSKBBK.pdf (https://www.perkeso.gov.my/images/lindung/lindung-24-jam/NewContributionRateIncludingSKBBK.pdf)

obligations.description: Record of a local employee’s release from SKBBK
obligations.trigger: A Malaysian citizen or permanent resident releases liability (Notis Perakuan Pelepasan Liabiliti) after the Cabinet decision of 8 July 2026
obligations.timing: From the release, stop the deduction for that employee (recorded as a NOT_REGISTERED SKBBK fact); foreign workers remain mandatory; the declaration window ran 13 July to 31 August 2026
obligations.authority: PERKESO, Skim Kemalangan Bukan Bencana Kerja (LINDUNG 24 Jam): “no longer compulsary for local employees … remains mandatory for foreign workers” (https://www.perkeso.gov.my/en/skim-kemalangan-bukan-bencana-kerja-lindung-24-jam.html)

obligations.description: Report of an employment injury to PERKESO
obligations.trigger: A work-related accident to an insured employee
obligations.timing: Within 48 hours of notification of the accident
obligations.authority: Employees’ Social Security Act 1969 (Act 4) Part IV (https://www.perkeso.gov.my/images/akta/ACT%204/Act%204%20-%20EMPLOYEES%E2%80%99%20SOCIAL%20SECURITY%20ACT%201969%20%28As%20at%201%20September%202022%29.pdf); PERKESO, Employer Registration (https://www.perkeso.gov.my/en/our-services/employer-employee/employer-registration.html)

obligations.description: Monthly employee contribution record
obligations.trigger: Every month
obligations.timing: Name, identity card number, occupation, contribution details, monthly wages and allowances for each employee
obligations.authority: PERKESO, Employer Registration (https://www.perkeso.gov.my/en/our-services/employer-employee/employer-registration.html)

obligations.description: Registration with HRD Corp (Form 1)
obligations.trigger: Ten or more Malaysian employees (compulsory); five to nine (optional)
obligations.timing: Within thirty days of becoming liable; the employer may not deduct the levy from wages
obligations.authority: Pembangunan Sumber Manusia Berhad Act 2001 ss.13-14, First Schedule; PSMB (Registration of Employers and Payment of Levy) Regulations reg. 4(1); HRD Corp Employers FAQ (https://web.archive.org/web/2026/https://hrdcorp.gov.my/faq)

obligations.description: HRD levy payment
obligations.trigger: Monthly wages of Malaysian employees (basic plus fixed allowances)
obligations.timing: By the 15th of the following month; 1% (compulsory) or 0.5% (optional); 10% a year interest for each day of default
obligations.authority: Pembangunan Sumber Manusia Berhad Act 2001 ss.13(1), 14; HRD Corp Employers FAQ (https://web.archive.org/web/2026/https://hrdcorp.gov.my/faq)

obligations.description: Monthly tax deduction (MTD/PCB) remittance with the MTD data (e-PCB, e-Data PCB or e-CP39)
obligations.trigger: MTD deducted from remuneration for the month, including CP38 instalments directed by LHDN
obligations.timing: On or before the 15th day of the following month; an employer who fails to deduct or remit is liable for the tax it failed to deduct
obligations.authority: Income Tax Act 1967 (Act 53) s.107(1)-(4) (https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/LOM/EN/Act%2053.pdf); Income Tax (Deduction from Remuneration) Rules 1994; LHDN, Employer’s Responsibility (https://www.hasil.gov.my/en/majikan/tanggungjawab-majikan/)

obligations.description: Notification of a new employee (CP22)
obligations.trigger: Commencing to employ an individual who is or is likely to be chargeable to tax
obligations.timing: Within thirty days after the employment commences, through e-CP22 (mandatory from 1 September 2024)
obligations.authority: Income Tax Act 1967 (Act 53) s.83(2) (https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/LOM/EN/Act%2053.pdf); LHDN, Notification of New Employees (https://www.hasil.gov.my/en/majikan/pemberitahuan-pekerja-baharu/)

obligations.description: Notification of cessation of employment (CP22A) and withholding of moneys
obligations.trigger: Cessation of employment of an employee who is retiring, is not subject to MTD with deduction made, or is leaving Malaysia permanently; death of an employee
obligations.timing: Not less than thirty days before the cessation (not more than thirty days after being informed of a death), through e-SPC; withhold money payable until ninety days after LHDN receives the notice or a tax clearance letter is received
obligations.owner: HR and Payroll / e-SPC submission and clearance letter
obligations.authority: Income Tax Act 1967 (Act 53) s.83(3), (5) (https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/LOM/EN/Act%2053.pdf); LHDN, Notification of Cessation of Employment (https://www.hasil.gov.my/en/majikan/pemberitahuan-pemberhentian-kerja/)

obligations.description: Notification of an employee leaving Malaysia for more than three months (CP21)
obligations.trigger: An employee chargeable to tax about to leave Malaysia for over three months
obligations.timing: Not less than thirty days before the expected departure, through e-SPC; withhold money payable where the employee leaves with no intention of returning until ninety days after receipt or clearance
obligations.authority: Income Tax Act 1967 (Act 53) s.83(4)-(5) (https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/LOM/EN/Act%2053.pdf); LHDN, Notification of Cessation of Employment (https://www.hasil.gov.my/en/majikan/pemberitahuan-pemberhentian-kerja/)

obligations.description: Statement of remuneration to each employee (Form EA)
obligations.trigger: Every employee paid in the calendar year
obligations.timing: On or before the last day of February of the following year
obligations.authority: Income Tax Act 1967 (Act 53) s.83(1A) (https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/LOM/EN/Act%2053.pdf); LHDN, Employer’s Responsibility (https://www.hasil.gov.my/en/majikan/tanggungjawab-majikan/)

obligations.description: Employer’s return (Form E) with C.P.8D
obligations.trigger: Every employer, each year
obligations.timing: On or before 31 March of the following year, by e-Filing (e-E); Form E is complete only with C.P.8D (or e-Data Praisi)
obligations.authority: Income Tax Act 1967 (Act 53) s.83(1) (https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/LOM/EN/Act%2053.pdf); LHDN, Employer’s Responsibility (https://www.hasil.gov.my/en/majikan/tanggungjawab-majikan/)

obligations.description: Statement of incentive payments to agents, dealers or distributors (CP58)
obligations.trigger: Cash or non-cash incentives paid to a non-employee agent, dealer or distributor
obligations.timing: On or before 31 March of the following year
obligations.authority: Income Tax Act 1967 (Act 53) s.83A (https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/LOM/EN/Act%2053.pdf); LHDN, Employer’s Responsibility (https://www.hasil.gov.my/en/majikan/tanggungjawab-majikan/)

obligations.description: Payroll tax records
obligations.trigger: Every year of assessment
obligations.timing: Kept for seven years and accessible to LHDN on request
obligations.authority: Income Tax Act 1967 (Act 53) s.82 (https://lom.agc.gov.my/ilims/upload/portal/akta/LOM/EN/Act%2053.pdf); LHDN, Employer’s Responsibility (https://www.hasil.gov.my/en/majikan/tanggungjawab-majikan/)

obligations.description: Employee relief (TP1), benefit-in-kind (TP2) and previous-employment (TP3) declarations
obligations.trigger: An employee elects to claim reliefs or rebates, or joins mid-year with prior remuneration
obligations.timing: Kept by the employer with the payroll records; a declared deduction is applied from the month it is declared and prior-employer TP3 figures from the month of joining
obligations.authority: LHDN, Specification for MTD Calculations Using Computerized Calculation 2026, sections D-E (https://www.hasil.gov.my/wp-content/uploads/spesifikasi-kaedah-pengiraan-berkomputer-pcb-2026.pdf)

obligations.description: Rest-day roster or fixed rest-day notice
obligations.trigger: Each month
obligations.timing: Before the commencement of the month in which the rest days fall; every roster preserved for six years
obligations.authority: Employment Act 1955 s.59(2)-(3) (https://jtksm.mohr.gov.my/sites/default/files/2023-11/Akta%20Kerja%201955%20(Akta%20265).pdf)

obligations.description: Notice of the six gazetted holidays chosen for the year
obligations.trigger: Each calendar year
obligations.timing: Exhibited conspicuously at the place of employment before the commencement of each calendar year
obligations.authority: Employment Act 1955 s.60D(1A) (https://jtksm.mohr.gov.my/sites/default/files/2023-11/Akta%20Kerja%201955%20(Akta%20265).pdf)

obligations.description: Daily, weekly and break limits, and permission to exceed them
obligations.trigger: Every schedule and attendance day
obligations.timing: Not more than 5 consecutive hours without 30 minutes' leisure, 8 hours a day (9 under proviso (iii)), a 10-hour spread-over and 45 hours a week; never more than 12 hours of work in a day outside the s.60A(2) emergencies; the Director General's written permission before contracting beyond s.60A(1)
obligations.authority: Employment Act 1955 s.60A(1), (1A), (2), (7) (https://jtksm.mohr.gov.my/sites/default/files/2023-11/Akta%20Kerja%201955%20(Akta%20265).pdf). The roster gate refuses a breaching schedule; payroll reports a breaching day

obligations.description: Work authorisation, privacy and workplace safety
obligations.trigger: Hiring, employment and termination
obligations.timing: Per the applicable instrument
obligations.owner: HR / applicable-law register, permits and retained evidence
obligations.authority: Separate compliance review required; these areas are not implemented by the payroll engine
